title: Commercial Fusion Energy 2026: From Tokamak Assembly to Tritium-Bred Architecture
subtitle: Six of nine ITER sector modules now sit in the pit [S4], so the binding constraint has shifted from assembly physics to tritium breeding and neutron-resistant materials [S2]

current_gaps.title: Net gain unproven
current_gaps.spec: No private developer has reached gain above one; NIF alone exceeds it

current_gaps.title: No tritium fuel cycle
current_gaps.spec: No closed loop: breeding blanket unbuilt, tritium decays in 12.3 years

current_gaps.title: Unqualified wall materials
current_gaps.spec: No neutron-resistant structural material or plasma-facing component qualified

current_gaps.title: Funding below authorization
current_gaps.spec: FY2027 FES appropriated $790M against $1.1B authorized ceiling; unresolved

current_gaps.title: Welding vs module schedule
current_gaps.spec: Sources conflict: bellows and vessel welding run five years, final module mid-2027

evolution_matrix.key_upgrade: Replaces between-shot manual parameter tuning with ML frameworks predicting shifts between shots at DIII-D [S3]
Replaces scarce purchased tritium, which decays with a half-life of about 12.3 years, with lithium breeding blankets driven by neutron radiation [S6][S2]
Replaces fission-qualified alloys with neutron-resistant structural materials and plasma-facing components set as roadmap milestones [S2]
Replaces one-off installation with a learning-curve module sequence: the sixth 1,100-tonne module lift took 30 hours and landed almost six months ahead of schedule [S4]
Replaces a tokamak-only portfolio with stellarators and high-temperature superconductors, the special focus of the IAEA outlook [S2][S5]

core_pillars.title: Tritium Fuel Cycle

core_pillars.title: Sector Assembly

core_pillars.title: Grid Deployment
core_pillars.concise_spec: Early plants by mid-2030s; $1.1B FES authorization vs $790M appropriated
